title: Zombie Outbreak: 30 Days Trapped on a Cruise Ship

voices.CAP: captain on the PA — older male, polite, filtered through ship speakers
voices.CG: Coast Guard radio — clipped male, band-passed + static
voices.R: Rosa Okafor, chief engineer — tired, sharp, warm underneath
voices.B: voice on the bridge — calm, unfamiliar male, filtered PA

note: The hero is 'you' and never speaks. 'reuse' = existing approved Brian take from the pilot (survival/vo).

scenes.title: DAY 1 — The message
lines: Day one. You're a waiter on a cruise ship. Three thousand passengers. Seven days at sea.
Then every phone on board buzzes at once. Stay in your cabins.
Ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain. Please return to your cabins. We are changing course to the nearest—
And the captain stops talking... mid-sentence.

scenes.title: Deck Five
lines: On Deck Five, people are walking strangely. Too slowly. And they're coming this way.
You learn the most important thing on this ship in the next ten seconds.
They don't see you. They hear you.

scenes.title: Rule number one
lines: Rule number one. Don't run to the lifeboats. Everyone else will.
You go down. To the one place nobody thinks about. The galley.

scenes.title: The galley
lines: Food for three weeks. Water for nine days. And one steel door.
You push a cart against the door... and you wait.
Rule number two. Be quiet. They follow sound.
That night, the engines stop. Nobody tells you why.

scenes.title: DAYS 2–5 — The rhythm
lines: Day three. You learn the ship's new rhythm.
Footsteps above you at noon. Something dragging at midnight. And long, long silences in between.
Day five. Someone has been in the cold room.
Half your bread is gone. And the infected don't close doors behind them.

scenes.title: DAY 7 — The night visitor
lines: Day seven. You wait in the dark to see who's stealing your food.
Whoever it is... knows this ship better than you do.

scenes.title: DAY 9 — The last bottle
lines: Day nine. The last bottle of water.
The nearest water is the ice machine in the crew mess. Forty steps down a dark corridor.
Unfortunately, the ice machine is the loudest thing on this ship.
This is the Coast Guard. All ports are closed. Any vessel carrying infected will not be allowed to reach the coast. We will use force.

scenes.title: Night 10 — The speakers
lines: That night, the speakers in the ceiling click on.
Nobody speaks. Someone is just... listening. Then they click off.

scenes.title: DAY 12 — The light
lines: Day twelve. Through the porthole... a light. A lighthouse. The ship has drifted toward land.
Then, deep below you... the engines start again.
And the ship turns away from land.
Someone else is alive on this ship. And they don't want to be rescued.

scenes.title: The service tunnel
lines: You could stay in the galley. Safe. Fed. And blind.
Or you could find out who's driving.
Rule number two works both ways.

scenes.title: Engine control
lines: Don't move. Hands where I can see them. Both of them.
You're the waiter. The one who hums when he's scared.
Turns out you weren't as quiet as you thought.
Day one, the bridge ordered all stop. Then the line went dead. Nobody's opened that door since.
Then the Coast Guard started sinking ships. So every time we drift too close to land... I start the engines and take us back out.
So that's who's driving. Not a ghost. A very tired engineer.

scenes.title: DAYS 13–29 — Two survivors
lines: Two survivors. One kitchen. One engine room.
She keeps the ship alive. You keep her fed.
Day twenty-nine. Fuel for one more day.
Tomorrow we pick a direction. And we don't come back.

scenes.title: DAY 30 — The bridge
lines: Steering just switched to the bridge. Nobody's been up there in thirty days.
Engine room. This is the bridge.
Thank you for keeping us alive. I'll take it from here.
Thirty days. You survived the outbreak, the hunger and the sea.
You found out who was driving. Now you just have to find out where he's taking you.
